column7: Accretion is the Astronomy Club of Sai University, created for students who are curious about the universe and want to explore astronomy and astrophysics beyond the classroom. The club brings together students with different levels of knowledge from those who simply enjoy looking at the night sky to those interested in the science behind stars, galaxies, black holes, and the universe itself. Through stargazing sessions, guest lectures, discussions, movie screenings, student-led talks, field trips, and astronomy-related activities, the club provides a space to learn, explore, and share our fascination with space.
column8: The main purpose of Accretion is to cultivate curiosity and scientific interest in astronomy and astrophysics among students. The club aims to make astronomy accessible and engaging while encouraging students to explore questions about the universe, develop observational skills, learn from experts, and engage in meaningful discussions with fellow enthusiasts. It also provides opportunities for students to share their own knowledge, experiences, and interests in astronomy.
column9: Students can expect a mix of hands-on experiences, learning opportunities, and informal activities. These include stargazing and Moon-gazing sessions using the club's telescope and binoculars, talks and seminars by astronomers and astrophysicists, student-led discussions, astronomy-themed movie screenings, and opportunities to attend astronomy-related events and field trips. Members can also contribute to astronomy discussions, share their own knowledge and experiences, and potentially participate in projects such as the club newsletter. Most importantly, the club offers a community of students who are genuinely curious about space and enjoy learning together.
column10: What makes Accretion unique is that it combines scientific learning with direct experiences of the night sky. Rather than limiting astronomy to lectures and discussions, the club gives students opportunities to actually observe celestial objects through its telescope and binoculars, interact with researchers and experts, and experience astronomy beyond campus through activities such as the visit to the Satish Dhawan Space Centre to witness a live rocket launch. The club also encourages students to become contributors—not just participants through member-led talks, discussions, writing, and other astronomy-related initiatives. It is a space where curiosity about the universe can turn into genuine exploration.
column11: Workshops, Competitions / Hackatons, Events, Talks/Guests Sessions
column13:
What makes Accretion unique is its involvement in the wider astronomy community beyond Sai University. The club is part of the core committee of ISAAC (Indian Synergy of Astronomy and Astrophysics Clubs), a pan-India collaboration connecting astronomy and astrophysics clubs across the country. As active members, we are currently contributing to the development of the ISAAC website and collaborating with other student astronomy communities.

The club has also received recognition beyond campus, with Accretion being featured in the June edition of Maan Ki Baat magazine. Alongside our stargazing sessions, expert talks, student-led discussions, field trips, and other activities, these initiatives give our members opportunities to engage with a broader astronomy community and contribute to it themselves.
column14:
We are looking for students who are curious about the universe and interested in exploring astronomy and astrophysics, regardless of their academic background or level of prior knowledge. You do not need to be an expert or have a background in physics to be part of Accretion.

Students who enjoy asking questions, observing the night sky, learning about space, participating in discussions, attending talks, or simply exploring something new will find a place in the club. Members can also explore areas such as observational astronomy, astrophysics, space science, astrophotography, scientific communication, and astronomy-related research and events.

Most importantly, we are looking for students who are willing to participate, learn, share their interests, and explore alongside others.

column17: No minimum technical skills or prior knowledge are required. An interest in astronomy and a willingness to learn and participate are the only requirements. column21:
After submitting the official Club Selection Form, shortlisted applicants will have a short, informal interaction with the club team. The interaction is not a test of technical knowledge. Instead, it is an opportunity for applicants to tell us why they would like to join Accretion, what interests them about astronomy or astrophysics, and what they hope to explore or contribute to the club.

We will primarily look for genuine curiosity, motivation, willingness to learn, communication, and interest in participating in club activities. Prior experience or technical knowledge is not required and will not be a deciding factor for beginners. Applicants can simply come prepared to have a conversation about their interests and enthusiasm for astronomy.

column7: The Oratory Club is about finding your voice and learning how to use it. It’s a space to speak, listen, question, and engage with ideas that matter. While debate is a part of what we do, the club goes beyond arguing a point; we want to explore the different ways people can express themselves and communicate effectively.
column8: Our main purpose is to help students become more confident and thoughtful speakers. We want to create a space where people can develop their ability to articulate ideas, think on their feet, and engage in meaningful conversations, regardless of how experienced they are.
column9: The club offers students opportunities to practise public speaking through debates, discussions, extempore speaking, workshops, and other activities. It also gives students a chance to engage with current and relevant issues, hear different perspectives, and learn from one another. Most importantly, it gives students a space to practise without feeling like they have to be a perfect speaker from the beginning.
column10: What makes us different is that we don’t believe oratory belongs only to people who are already confident or good at debating. We welcome people at every level and focus on helping each person develop their own style of speaking. We want members to leave not just as better speakers, but as people who are more willing to question, listen, think, and speak up.
column11: Workshops, Competitions / Hackatons, Training Sessions, Performances, Events, Talks/Guests Sessions, Discussions, Inter-College Events
column14:
Students who are curious, outspoken, or even just curious about becoming more outspoken would enjoy the club. You don’t have to be confident or experienced in public speaking to join; being willing to participate and try is enough.

The club is a good fit for students who enjoy discussing ideas, keeping up with what’s happening around them, questioning different perspectives, or simply want to become better at expressing themselves. It’s also a space for students who want to work on confidence, communication, critical thinking, spontaneity, and the ability to think on their feet.

Whether someone enjoys debating, storytelling, extempore speaking, discussions, or simply wants to get comfortable speaking in front of others, there’s room for them here. Ultimately, we’re looking for students who are curious, open-minded, willing to listen, and willing to find their own voice.
column21:
The selection process is simple and is mainly an opportunity for us to get to know how you communicate and express yourself. Applicants can expect a short, interactive speaking activity where you may be given a topic or question on the spot and asked to share your thoughts. We’re not looking for perfect speeches or professional debaters; we’re more interested in how you think, respond, communicate, and engage with others.

And don’t worry if public speaking makes you nervous. The whole point is to help you become more comfortable with speaking and find your own voice. If you’re unable to attend the selection in person, you can also submit a short video of yourself speaking on a topic of your choice.
